artifacts.summary: Research for the canonical certificate-wire printer, total parser and round-trip theorem: twelve probe-confirmed defects in the current parser (including silent misdecoding of \t, \r and \uXXXX), the reason no theorem is provable against the existing partial defs, a recommended two-layer codec design, and a green sorry-free 147-line proof spike validating the technique.

147-line sorry-free spike: mutual-inductive canonical JSON value, canonical printer, fuel-indexed total parser, and the prefix round-trip theorem; compiles green, #print axioms reports only [propext, Quot.sound]. The skeleton the implementation should follow.
Twelve executable probes recording the current parser's observed behaviour on adversarial and ordinary-but-unusual input; the source of the D1-D12 table in the report.

user_decision.question: How should the canonical wire codec handle JSON \uXXXX escapes, which Python's json.dumps emits by default (ensure_ascii=True) and which the current Lean parser silently misdecodes into a different atom name?
options: Reject \uXXXX with a protocol error, and pin ensure_ascii=False in the joint canonical contract — requires a one-line change in the producing repository
Implement \uXXXX decoding correctly, including surrogate pairs, so the producing side may keep Python's default — no change needed there, but a larger and harder-to-prove escape layer here
user_decision.recommended: Reject \uXXXX with a protocol error, and pin ensure_ascii=False in the joint canonical contract — requires a one-line change in the producing repository
